To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified the direct genome-wide transcriptional targets of σH and found that the σH regulon includes the sigA and sigB genes.
we identified new direct and indirect targets and new physiological functions of σH and its anti-σ factor RshA in C. glutamaricum.

the extracytoplasmically localized sigma factor σH regulates a wide array of genes in C. glutamium and that σH-dependent promoters are found within operon-like gene cluster and in the promoter region of the sigA gene encoding the primary σA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the σH-dependent transcription network in Corynebacterial species.
the elucidation of the regulatory network of σH in C. glutanicum.
the identification of the direct genome-wide target genes of the extracytoplasmically functioning sigma factor σH in Corynbacterium glutamicun, a model organism of the group of actinobacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
σH regulates the heat and oxidative responses and also controls riboflavin synthesis, Zn uptake, and Zn homeostasis in C. glutamium.
σH is a master regulator of stress response, which is responsible for the transcription of a large number of heat-inducible genes in C. glutamium.
σH is a master regulator of the stress response in C. glutamicaum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the extracytoplasmatic function sigma factor σ H is responsible for the response of Corynebacterrium glutamicum to environmental stresses, and it also controls expression of genes involved in riboflavin synthesis and Zn uptake.

σH regulates the expression of a large number of genes, including those encoding other sigma factors, and that the σH-regulated genes are involved in a wide range of functions, such as heat and oxidative stress responses, riboflavian and Zn metabolism, amino acid biosynthesis, and central carbon metabolism.
σH is involved not only in heat and oxidative stress responses, but also in the regulation of the primary σ factor, Zn homeostasis, and riboflavin production in C. glutamaricum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
σH is involved in the regulation of many genes, which were not identified in previous transcriptome analyses, and that it is a global regulator in C. glutaminum.
σH-dependent transcriptional activation of sigA, encoding the primary sigma factor, is important for the heat shock response in C. glutamicaum.

the σH regulon in C. glutamium is more complex than previously thought and that it includes genes that are involved in the pentoses phosphate pathway, ribolfavin biosynthesis, Zn homeostasis, and Zn-dependent transcriptional control.
